story_text:
You will not find expensive 3D concepts or jazzy studio illustrations on this page. Why? Because Born to Joy Works is starting from absolute ground zero. Every single penny of our budget is being reserved for the actual physical lease and the production software—not for hiring expensive graphic designers to make a page look pretty.
We are building an independent animation studio at Dagenham Dock in place of the former Barking Power Stationin the UK from scratch. What we lack in corporate artwork, we make up for in a massive pipeline of completed, original stories ready for production. By backing this project, you are funding the raw foundation of a new creative hub.
But to be fair, I'll tell you what original stories I plan to release from the pipeline of my studio: Sonic The Hedgehog's happy ending, an animated Bible multi season saga but through the lenses of Kabbalah, some Disney Princes stories (the classic Disney Princess stories book but from the perspective of the princes), an anime take on the North Korean Gulags and so much more CGI vitality to come!
(The image above should be a major hint of what's to come to the large screen!)
risks: Real estate is incredibly expensive and fast-moving. If we try to take out a massive, traditional commercial lease on a building immediately, legal fees and upfront deposits will completely wipe out our starting budget before we even open the doors. Our Solution: We are completely bypassing traditional landlords. We will use this initial budget to secure dedicated, private office space inside premium, design-led creative serviced hubs (like Spaces or specialized tech co-working networks). This gives Born to Joy Works a physical address, high-speed fiber internet, and elite presentation spaces on day one without risking a single penny on long-term legal deadlocks. This campaign page is an empty canvas with no flashy 3D concept designs or glossy character posters. The risk is that backers cannot "see" what we are building yet. Our Solution: The moment this campaign succeeds, we will deploy our core animation software suites. We will use our private backer update feed to post raw, weekly behind-the-scenes video logs. You will watch us walk into the physical space, unbox the tech, and transform our text scripts into storyboards and layout animatics in real time. Our lack of initial visuals becomes a shared building experience. When you are balancing a physical space layout with software deployment, running out of money due to poor budgeting is always a threat. Our Solution: We are running on a strict, phased rollout strategy. We will not spend capital on secondary expansions or hiring until our baseline physical desk space and core animation workstation are fully set up, tested, and operational. By keeping our overheads completely locked down, we ensure the studio's foundation is structurally permanent.
